source.name: MPD Public Safety Incidents (Memphis Police Department NIBRS-coded incident feed)
source.where: Offense_Datetime >= DATE '2024-01-01 00:00:00' AND Offense_Datetime < DATE '2025-01-01 00:00:00' AND City = 'MEMPHIS'

worker_judgment_notes: Source is the Memphis Police Department's public 'MPD_Public_Safety_Incidents' ArcGIS hosted feature layer (identity-verified 2026-07-08, City field domain confirms 213,091/213,896 2024 rows are City=='MEMPHIS' after trimming/case-normalizing, with the remainder being small leakage into CORDOVA (648, an unincorporated Shelby County community often mailed as Memphis), ARLINGTON (37), BARTLETT (18), null (98), GERMANTOWN/LAKELAND (1 each), and a 'MEMPHPIS' typo (2) plus an 8-row leading-space ' MEMPHIS' variant -- all excluded by the exact City='MEMPHIS' server-side where-clause filter). Schema exposes true NIBRS incident codes directly in UCR_Incident_Code (56 distinct codes covering the full 213,896-row 2024 total exactly, cross-checked against the separate UCR_Description field which is 1:1 with UCR_Incident_Code) -- standard 6-offense NIBRS-code mapping used: 09A->murder (excludes 09B negligent manslaughter, 09C justifiable homicide, and a locally-added 09D 'NEGL VEHICULAR MSLTR' vehicular-manslaughter code, none of which are 09A), 120->robbery, 13A->aggravated_assault (excludes 13B simple assault and 13C intimidation), 220->burglary, 240->motor_vehicle_theft, and larceny is the full standard NIBRS 23A-H series (23A pocket-picking, 23B purse-snatching, 23C shoplifting, 23D theft from building, 23E theft from coin-op machine, 23F theft from motor vehicle, 23G theft of MV parts/accessories, 23H all other larceny). RAPE IS NOT MAPPED: zero 11A/11B/11C (or any 36-series) codes appear anywhere in the full distinct UCR_Incident_Code list for this layer across all years, not just 2024 -- this is a total source omission of sex offenses (matches the pre-registration brief's documented expectation and the same accepted DC/Denver/Jacksonville pattern), not a taxonomy judgment call; rape stays unadmitted for Memphis regardless, consistent with repo rape default-deny texture policy. CRITICAL DATA-QUALITY FINDING -- duplicate rows from a view fan-out, fixed by the dedup key, not a taxonomy problem: this FeatureServer is a hosted ArcGIS VIEW (isView=true/isUpdatableView=true per its service metadata), and empirically ~45-55% of offense rows are exact duplicates of another row sharing the same (Crime_ID, UCR_Incident_Code, Offense_Datetime, Reported_Datetime, Street_Address, Latitude, Longitude) but with a DIFFERENT ObjectId and Source_ObjectID (verified by pulling all 474 raw 09A/murder rows and finding only 241 distinct Crime_IDs, with per-Crime_ID row-multiplicity of 1/2/3 and, for 136 of 241 groups, byte-identical content across every field except ObjectId/Source_ObjectID -- almost certainly an underlying multi-snapshot/export-batch union in the hosted view, not real repeat charges). Deduping on (Crime_ID, UCR_Incident_Code) -- which correctly collapses these exact-content duplicate export copies while still preserving legitimately distinct offenses within the same incident (e.g. a burglary row and a separate larceny row sharing one Crime_ID are NOT collapsed) -- was validated against official controls (state/controls/jurisdiction_controls_2024.parquet, TNMPD0000, cius_publication_annual, 12/12 months reported, quality_tier high, and independently corroborated by reported_count_nibrs matching reported_count_cius almost exactly for every offense, so this is not a masked-reporting-gap situation on the controls side): after City filter + this dedup, murder 241/249=0.968, robbery 2151/2138=1.006, burglary 5444/5616=0.969, larceny 27511/26978=1.020, motor_vehicle_theft 9789/9711=1.008 -- all five reconcile within ~3.2%, which is strong independent confirmation the duplicate-row hypothesis and dedup key are correct (before this fix, undeduped feed-vs-control ratios ran a uniform and misleading ~1.85-1.97x high across every one of these five offenses). AGGRAVATED ASSAULT IS FLAGGED, NOT FORCE-RECONCILED: even after the identical dedup, aggravated_assault comes out to 7454 against a control of 12522 (ratio 0.595, a genuine ~40% shortfall, not a duplication artifact -- the same per-Crime_ID multiplicity distribution as murder/robbery/burglary/larceny/MVT was confirmed present in the 13A rows, ruling out under-deduping as the cause). The most plausible mechanism, not verified against an official MPD statement and reported here as a flagged ambiguity rather than a guess baked into the mapping: many public-facing municipal crime-incident maps (including some noted elsewhere in this repo's source inventory) redact or omit domestic-violence-flagged incidents from the public feed to protect victim location privacy, and aggravated assault is disproportionately composed of domestic-violence incidents relative to murder/robbery/burglary/larceny/MVT -- this would produce exactly the selective ~40% aggravated-assault-only shortfall observed here with no comparable effect on the other five mapped offenses. This is left as an open, reported gap; aggravated_assault is not force-adjusted or excluded from the mapping, and the strict 10% reconciliation gate will fail it on the merits (real, not a mapping bug). Bounds are the raw TIGER/crosswalk-touching Memphis block-group envelope (546 BGs) padded by ~0.05 degrees. Contract is share-lane only per the standard generic-runner convention; the strict 10% reconciliation gate decides feed-total-candidate status per offense, not admission of this contract at all.
